# Data

**Everything in this folder is synthetic.** It was generated by `python/generate_data.py` with a fixed random seed (42). It is not real company data and no figure here describes real business performance.

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| `raw/` | five source CSVs with **deliberately injected data-quality defects**, plus `defect_manifest.json` (exactly what was injected) |
| `processed/` | cleaned tables for SQL / Power BI / Python, plus `dim_date.csv`, `fact_sales.csv`, `cleaning_log.csv`, `cleaning_summary.json`, `rejected_rows.csv` |

Column-level documentation: [`../docs/data_dictionary.md`](../docs/data_dictionary.md). Cleaning rules: [`../docs/business_rules.md`](../docs/business_rules.md#cleaning-rules).

## Expected row counts (seed 42)

| Table | Raw | Processed |
|---|---:|---:|
| regions | 22 | 22 |
| products | 69 | 69 |
| customers | 2,207 | 2,200 |
| orders | 17,111 | 16,990 |
| order_items | 31,840 | 31,540 |
| dim_date | n/a | 731 |
| fact_sales | n/a | 31,540 |
| rejected_rows | n/a | 258 |

After loading into MySQL (`sql/01_create_schema.sql`) the six table counts at the end of the script must match the processed column.

## Regenerate

```bash
pip install -r python/requirements.txt
python python/generate_data.py          # writes data/raw (seed 42; use --seed N for a different dataset)
python python/clean_data.py             # writes data/processed
python python/validate_data.py          # checks keys, domains, dates, reconciliation and the cleaning log
```

The same seed always produces byte-identical raw files (`tests/test_data_quality.py` asserts this). Other seeds produce a different but equally valid dataset, and the validation and tests still pass, but the numbers quoted in the README and `docs/powerbi_reference_values.md` apply to seed 42 only. After changing the seed re-run `python python/generate_insights.py --update-readme`.

## What was injected into the raw files

22 defect types, 2,437 injected cells or rows in total. Examples: duplicate order, line and customer rows; order dates as `dd/mm/yyyy` or `dd-Mon-yyyy`; status spellings such as `Canceled`; ship dates before order dates; missing customer ids, channels, unit costs; zero or negative quantities; negative or blank prices; discounts entered as whole percentages; unknown product ids; order lines pointing to orders that do not exist. The full list with counts is in `raw/defect_manifest.json`.

## Privacy

Customer names are random combinations of common first and last names. There are no emails, phone numbers, addresses, government identifiers or payment data.
